corpus: tests/markdown_paste_corpus/ -- round-1/ and round-2/ are byte copies of the two native rounds' corpora (copiedFrom; both rounds' SHA256SUMS verify); m0/ holds the items spec 11 M0 adds (NUL, invalid UTF-8, List<T>, task list, entities, parse failure), X13 (rule order), and X15-X17 (the RFC 3629 classes spec 12.1 names). rules.source: spec 9.14 (three scan rules), 10.4 (NUL, encoding, md_parse failure), 12.1 (valid UTF-8; labels TOO_LARGE and INVALID_UTF8; PARSE_FAIL by injection), and the task brief's 'Engine reply' (handoff/tasks/TASK-2026-10-16-v21-implementation.md), which fixes the order.
rules.orderNote: First rule that fires gives the verdict. NUL, INVALID_UTF8, TOO_LARGE, PARSE_FAIL and NO_BLOCK are all INVALID_ARGUMENT (code 1). Codes 2 (MARKDOWN_ENCODING_UNSUPPORTED) and 3 (MARKDOWN_NEEDS_CARET) come between code 1 and REMOTE in the engine but are not properties of the bytes: every verdict here assumes a UTF-8 thread encoding and a collapsed caret. NO_BLOCK and REMOTE/HTML can never both hold (an image span or HTML needs a block), so only REMOTE-before-HTML is an observable order; X13 pins it.

NUL.when: a byte 0x00 anywhere in the input

INVALID_UTF8.when: the input is not valid UTF-8 by RFC 3629: an overlong form, a surrogate (U+D800-U+DFFF), a value above U+10FFFF, a byte that cannot start a sequence, or a truncated sequence

TOO_LARGE.when: more than 65,536 bytes (the engine's hard limit)

PARSE_FAIL.when: md_parse returns non-zero; no input bytes cause it in md4c 0.5.3, so it is produced by allocation-failure injection in the native model test only (item field 'inject')

NO_BLOCK.when: md4c enters no block other than MD_BLOCK_DOC

REMOTE.when: any MD_SPAN_IMG whose src does not start with "data:", compared case-insensitively

PASS.when: no rule fires; the engine dispatches

rules.dispatched: false for every verdict except PASS
